idiom_name: component-local useState/useReducer in the component that reads the value (React); closest-common-parent lifting for state a sibling needs
implementation_notes: In React the state cell is a hook call inside the component that uses it: useState (or useReducer) declares the value, and React re-renders the component whose state changed and its children, so moving state down physically shrinks the subtree that an update can reach - the mechanism the pattern exploits. The replacement for the classic structure (all state in one store or at the root) is therefore a local hook cell plus deliberate lifting: state that a sibling needs moves to the closest common parent and is passed down while an updater callback is passed up, and shared state that belongs to distant consumers goes into a provider mounted as low as those consumers allow. Keep genuinely global state (session, server cache, cross-route data) in a store, and keep transient UI state out of it; the root-lifted form remains justified exactly there.
pitfalls: Hooks must be called at the top level of the component (or of another hook), never inside conditions, loops or callbacks; stateful logic needed in a branch belongs in its own component or hook.
State is identified by position in the tree: moving a colocated cell into a component that remounts on every parent render (wrong key, conditional wrapper) resets it silently.

Colocated state cannot be read by a parent; when the parent needs it the value must be lifted with callbacks (or the parent made to render the child), otherwise the temptation is to reach for refs and create hidden coupling.
